source.title: RIGA at SemEval-2022 Task 1: Scaling Recurrent Neural Networks for CODWOE Dictionary Modeling
source.authors: Eduards Mukans; Gus Strazds; Guntis Bārzdiņš

record.tranche_reason: It tests epoch-wise double descent using recurrent models on definition modeling, a different model family and task from the original settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-size sweeps in Tables 2–4, but these are CODWOE quality scores rather than test error and do not establish an interpolation threshold or a model-wise double-descent curve. They are retained as limited model-size performance results. It reports epoch-wise validation accuracy, cross-entropy and automatic-metric findings; no training-sample-size sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: Trains GRU definition-modeling models long past overfitting and tracks validation accuracy and loss over epochs to check for epoch-wise double descent. This is a new setting (recurrent NLP models) with a direct result on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that scaling GRUs in depth or width improves performance (H2, 'tentatively' confirmed on small models). They base the confirmation of epoch-wise double descent (H3) partly on informal human judgement of Table 5 glosses.
record.recipe_differences: Tests GRU definition modeling on CODWOE rather than the original study settings; tracks validation token accuracy, cross-entropy and task-specific automatic scores. The competition data amount was fixed.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported epoch-wise effect depends on model depth/size: it is clear for the 4-layer model, while the 1- and 2-layer models are described as too small for the effect.
record.problems: The model-size experiments cover only relatively small models and do not report an interpolation threshold. The epoch-wise plots provide no numeric values in the text. Evaluation is mainly on a trial dataset consisting of only 200 glosses; human evaluation is described as informal.

untested.parts: Only 3–4 sizes per sweep, with no interpolation threshold and no fall-rise-fall analysis. The authors frame the size results as monotone scaling (H2), not model-wise double descent.
Validation token accuracy is under teacher forcing. No numeric curves are given and there is no label-noise variation. A single task and architecture family is used.
Data amount fixed by the competition; no sample-size sweep.

missing.what: Per-example gloss outputs and MoverScore at epochs 5, 193 and 315 for the 4-layer model. Authors cite this table for continued improvement after the first spike, but the per-example MoverScores are mixed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label was dropped: the size tables neither locate an interpolation threshold nor show the curve, so V1 is untested here, not qualified. All V2 evidence is figure-only or prose, with no numeric values. The evaluation set is small: validation data for Figure 1 and a 200-gloss trial set for Figure 2.

versions.untested_parts: The reported model-size results cover relatively small configurations and do not identify a just-fitting threshold or measure the complete fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
The reported curves are on validation data and the task's automatic metrics, not a broad range of datasets or model families.
No training-data-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes or general capacity sweep through interpolation.
No unified effective-complexity measure or comparison of peak locations across axes.
No label-noise or regularization sweep, or test of multiple peaks.
No effective-parameter recounting or test of whether that turns the curve into a U-shape.

relationships.condition: 4-layer GRU, hidden 3072, validation accuracy and cross-entropy
relationships.reason: Authors state the 4-layer model 'shows a clear epoch-wise double descent effect', and the abstract reports it for cross-entropy (epoch-acc-4, epoch-ce). The evidence is figure or text only.
relationships.display_finding: The four-layer model showed clear epoch-wise double descent in validation token accuracy; cross-entropy double descent was reported without specifying the model configuration.
